map.VO2max 50 ml/kg/min、体重 70 kg、全力运动 90 秒（*: VO2max 50 ml/kg/min, body weight 70 kg, 90 sec all-out exercise (**1.5 minutes**), average oxygen uptake 45 ml/kg/min -> theoretical demand 50×70×1.5÷1000 = 5.25 L, actual uptake 45×70×1.5÷1000 = 4.73 L, accumulated oxygen deficit 0.53 L, MAOD = 0.53÷70×1000 ≈ 7.5 ml/kg (weak). **Key: duration must first be converted from seconds to minutes**; treating 90 as minutes would give 315 L of demand and 450 ml/kg — dozens of times beyond physiological limits.

map.MAOD=(VO2max−运动中平均摄氧)×时长(分钟)，本例差值只有 5 ml: MAOD = (VO2max − average oxygen uptake during exercise) × duration (minutes). Here the difference is only 5 ml/kg/min over 1.5 minutes ⇒ 7.5 ml/kg is normal. A higher deficit requires a larger "demand − uptake" gap (near supramaximal intensity) or a longer time to exhaustion; the reference standard of >= 70 ml/kg usually comes from supramaximal tests lasting 2-3 minutes or more, where uptake is far below demand.
